claims.text: AuthController at stage-1 takes DonHangDbContext and JwtTokenService in its constructor; Login looks up the customer by email with db.Customers.FirstOrDefaultAsync and checks the password with PasswordHasher.Verify from DonHang.Domain, returning 401 on failure.

OrdersController.Create reads the customer id from the token, builds OrderItems from the request, calls orderService.PlaceOrderAsync and returns CreatedAtAction (201); it does not query the database directly.
ProductsController at stage-1 takes DonHangDbContext and queries db.Products directly in List and Get; neither method applies a business rule.
A layer violation is worth a review comment even when the code works; tests check behavior, not placement; misplaced code erodes the one-reason-to-change separation one PR at a time.
Moving misplaced code is cheaper at review time than after merge, when other changes may already depend on it.

self_check.notes: Retargeted to stage-1 (DECISIONS.md §3). Outline item 2 read as 'a rule in a repository' (query logic belongs in the repository). No invented violation code; the login endpoint is framed as an imagined PR. No comment-labelling ritual (depth_notes).
